answer: The caulker drives oakum into every seam of the hull and the record holds the seam, the date and the caulker's mark. A willow hull claimed as caulked fails the record: the oakum must have been driven at the ridge of the hull, and a hull never caulked leaks at the first lock. Buying a false caulking record costs 18,300 in bribes to the caulker and a forged yard book, while the dawn record is read at every docking, so a seam whose caulking was never entered is found by the water in the bilge.
